body.p: The Office Action addresses and rejects claims 1, 4-5, 7-10, 13-14, and 16-18 Reconsideration is respectfully requested.
Claims 2-3, 6, 11-12, and 15 are canceled without prejudice or disclaimer.

Claims 1 and 10 are amended as indicated above. Support for these amendments can be found throughout the specification and drawings, for example, at least in FIGS. 6, 8 and in paragraphs [0023]-[0024], [0033], [0036], [0040], [0042], [0047], [0056], [0060]-[0062] of the published application. No new matter is added.

Applicants thank the Examiner for the courtesy of the telephonic Interview conducted on August 14, 2024 with Applicants' representative Michael Mattoni ("the Interview"). During the Interview, the claim rejections under 35 U.S.C. §§ 101 and 103 and proposed claim amendments were discussed. Agreement was reached that the proposed amendments, presented herewith, appear to overcome the rejections, subject to further search and consideration.
The Office Action rejects claims 1, 4-5, 7-10, 13-14, and 16-18 under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as allegedly being directed to a judicial exception without significantly more. Office Action, pp. 3-5.
As indicated above, agreement was reached in the Interview that the proposed claim
amendments, presented herewith, appear to overcome this rejection, subject to further search and consideration.

Accordingly, claims 1 and 10 recites patent-eligible subject matter. Claims 4-5, 7-10, 13-14, and 16-18 variously depend from claims 1 and 10 and also recite patent eligible subject matter at least due to their dependency from a patent-eligible claim.

The Office Action rejects claims 1, 4-5, 7-10, 13-14, and 16-18 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over U.S. 2020/0133261 to Tao et al. ("Tao") in view of U.S. 2014/0025746 to Rhee et al. ("Rhee"), U.S. 2022/0417359 to Tokuyama ("Tokuyama"), and U.S. 2011/0215900 to Corradino et al. ("Corradino"). Office Action, pp. 5-11.
As indicated above, agreement was reached in the Interview that the proposed claim
amendments, presented herewith, appear to overcome this rejection, subject to further search and consideration.

Accordingly, claims 1 and 10 distingiush over Tao, Rhee, Tokuyama, and Corradino, alone or in any combination, and represent allowable subject matter. Claims 4-5, 7-10, 13-14, and 16-18 variously depend from claims 1 and 10 and also represent allowable subject matter at least due to their dependency from a patent-eligible claim.

In conclusion, Applicants submit that all pending claims are in condition for allowance for at least the reasons discussed above, and allowance thereof is respectfully requested. Applicants' amendment of the claims does not constitute a concession that the claims are not allowable in their unamended form. The Examiner is encouraged to telephone the undersigned Agent for Applicants if such communication is deemed to expedite prosecution of this application.

A two (2) month extension of time is believed to be due with this submission. However, in the event that a petition for further extension of time is required to be submitted at this time, Applicants hereby petition under 37 C.F.R. § 1.136(a) for an extension of time for as many months as are required to ensure that the above-identified application does not become abandoned.

All fees due in connection with this submission are believed to be paid. However, if necessary, the Director is hereby authorized to charge any deficiency in the fees filed with this paper, asserted to be filed with this paper, or which should have been filed with this paper, to our Deposit Account No. 50-1943, under Order No. 347836.00101.
